rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE THIRD ENGINEERING DISTRICT IN THE PROVINCE OF BATANGAS, TO BE LOCATED IN THE CITY OF LIPA, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: "Sustainable Government Resettlement Areas Act" Rationale: The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) has a temporary sub-district engineering office in Lipa city which aims to lighten up the heavy word load of Batangas 2nd Engineering Office, its existence is temporary in nature. However, its existence is temporary in nature and will not be able to address the growing infrastructure needs brought about by the passage of the R.A. 7916.> In order that this difficulty be resolved, a thirdengineering district office must be established which will solely cater to the engineering needs of the fourth congressional district composed of the municipalities of Padre Garcia, Taysan, Ibaan, San Jose, Rosario and San Juan and the city of Lipa.. > Gives the details of these required needs for all resettlement areas: (1) educational and health facilities; (2) provision of basic community amenities and social services; (3) industrial zones; and (4) use of lots in the industrial area/zone.

rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING FURTHER WORKERS' RIGHT TO UNIONIZE BY DISALLOWING THE FORMATION OF LABOR-MANAGEMEN T COUNCILS OR SIMILAR BODIES IN ORGANIZED COMPANIES, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE ARTICLE 277 (H) OF THE LABOR CODE
rows.abstract: Proposes the following amendments to Art. 277 (H) of the Labor Code: "Art. 277. Miscellaneous provisions. - (a) xxx (b) xxx (c) xxx (d) xxx (e) xxx (f) xxx (g) xxx (h) In establishments where no legitimate labor organization exists, labor-management committees may be formed voluntarily by workers and employers for the purpose of promoting industrial peace.  IN NO CASE SHALL BE FORMATION OF LABOR-MANAGEMEN T COUNCILS OR SIMILAR BODIES BE ALLOWED IN ORGANIZED COMPANIES. PROVIDED, HOWEVER THAT [T] the Department of Labor and Employment shall endeavor to enlighten and educate the workers THROUGH THEIR UNIONS and employeess on their rights and responsibilitie s through labor education with emphasis on the policy thrusts of this Code."

rows.abstract: Rationale: This Bill seeks to provide a separation pay of at least one (1) month pay for every year of service to every resigning employee who has rendered at least ten (10) years of service with his company. Needless to state, the separation pay hereby proposed is designed as a sort of longevity compensation and award for the measure of loyalty and finally, to provide the resigning employee the imemdiate wherewithal dduring the period of separation.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO REQUIRE A DETAILED AND UNIFORM DISCLOSURE OF INFORMATION IN CONNECTION WITH APPLICATION AND SOLICITATION OF CREDIT AND CHARGE CARDS AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: "Fair Credit and Charge Card Disclosure Act of 1997" Provides for the following --- (1) the annual percentage rate applicable to extension of credit.  Where more than one rate applies, the card issuer must also disclose the balances or range of balances to which each rate applies; (2) the annual or other periodic membership fee on the issuance or availability of credit or charge cards and any transaction charge for use of the card to purchase goods and services; (3) the grace of free period during which a cardholder may repay the balance without incurring a finance charge; and (4) the name of the balance calculation method used by the card issuer.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO REGULATE THE PRACTICE OF PHYSICAL THERAPY IN THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The controversy surrounding the 1996 physical therapy and occupational therapy examination placed in bad light the integrity of the Members of the Board of Examiners and the Professional Regulation Commission. The incident runs counter to the aspiration of the present administration for an ethical government which is the component of the culture of excellence in our bureaucracy through the concerted efforts from all sectors to demand and insist on quality and honesty in public service. "Philippine Physical Therapy Law" Aims to --- (1) improve the quality of physical therapy education in the country; (2) create and strengthen the Board of Physical Therapy which will be tasked to maintain highly professional, ethical and technical standards;; and provide for a COUNCIL OF PHYSICAL THERAPY EDUCATION, separate and distinct from that of the Occupational Therapy Education.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING THE ORGANIC FERTILIZER INDUSTRY, PLACING TOTAL BAN ON THE USE OF SYNTHETIC FERTILIZERS, PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The ultiate concern here is to improve and maintain the physical, chemical and biological properties of the soil without sacrificing its productivity. States the following --- 'SECTION 2. Total Ban. - It is hereby declared that there is atotal ban on the use of inorganic and synthetic fertilizers in all agricultural farms, owned either by the government or private individuals and/or corporations, whoch are engaged in agricultural farming.

rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING THE RIGHTS OF PATIENTS AND PRESCRIBING PENALTIES  FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF
rows.abstract: Rationale: In the Philippines, there is yet a law to be created to protect, promote and defend the rights off patients.  We hear horriying stories  of patients who died or are further injured in hospitals as a result of negligence and incompetence of their supposed healers. "Magna Carta of Patients' Rights Act" Declares it the policy of the State to ensure and protect the rights of patientss to decent, humane, and quality health care. States the RIGHTS OF PATIENTS, such as the right to: (1) MEDICAL CARE AND HUMANE TREATMENT; (2) INFORMED CONSENT; (3) PRIVACY; (4) PRIVILEGED COMMUNICATION; etc.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 1997-02-18

rows.author: A081
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING THAT THE SALARY OF GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES WHO HAVE RENDERED AT LEAST TWENTY (20) YEARS OF CONTINUOUS GOVERNMENT SERVICE SHALL BE ADJUSTED TO ONE SALARY GRADE HIGHER
rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill therefore seeks to adjust the salary grade by one salary grade higher of those who have served the government for at least twenty years. This is in consonance with Article II, Section 9 of the 1987 Constitution which states that: "The State shall promote a just and dynamic social order that will ensure the prosperity and independence of the nation and free the people from poverty through policies that provide adequate social services, promote full employment, a rising standard of living, and an improved quality life for all."

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THAT EVERY GOVERNMENT RESETTLEMENT AREA MUST HAVE ITS OWN INDUSTRIAL AREA/ZONE, EDUCATIONAL AND HEALTH FACILITIES, AND OTHER BASIC COMMUNITY AMENITIES AND SOCIAL SERVICES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: At present, many Filipinos are living in resettlements areas provided for either by the government or the private sector. Resettlement takes these people away from their major source of livelihood. This causes them to become nonfunctioning assets of the society because of the lack of sufficient jobs in their new community. It is therefore  in keeping with the mandate of the Constitution to provide a community acceptable to these relocatees and with adequate employment opportunities as well. "Sustainable Government Resettlement Areas Act" Explains the details of the following requirements for all resettlement areas: (1) education and health facilities; (2) provision of basic community amenities and social services; (3) industriall zones; and (4) use of lots in the industrial area/zone.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOCATING FUNDS FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF A SIX-YEAR (6 YR.) FEEDING PROGRAM FOR CHILDREN AND A NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAM FOR PARENTS NATIONWIDE
rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill seeks therefore to implement a feeding program for pre-school and primary school children and nutrition education for parents to arrest the problem of malnutrition. The feed program is also expected to encourage parents to sendtheir children to school which would reduce the high drop out rate now being experienced. The intervention is graduated and limited to a period of six years to preclude dependency among local governments. Explains the NUTRITION PROGRAM proposed in this Act; prescribes the allocation of FUNDS for this purpose as follows:  SEC. 3 Extent. Funds shall be made available to barangays to the extent as follows: (1) Barangays in 6th class municipalites - 100%: (2) Barangays in 5th class municipalities -90%; (3) Barangays in 4th class municipalities - 80%; (4) Barangays in 3rd class municipalities - 70%; (5) Barangays in 2nd class municipalities - 60%; and (6) barangays in 1st class municipalities - 50%.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE NATIONAL SERVICE PROGRAM (NSP) FOR ALL STUDENTS IN HIGHER EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS
rows.abstract: Rationale: For decades, there has been a clamor from all sectors of the academic community to make education responsive to the changes that occur in society and relevant to the needs of the times. While values re-orientation has been injected into various subjects, efforts failed to gain appreciation by the students because the teaching of these concepts remain to be limited in the classrooms. In this light, it has become necessary to redirect the students to the ethics of civic and social responsibility by incorporating experiential activities in the curriculum, activities which will be udnertaken in the communities. "National Students SErvice Program Act of 1997" Shall cover all able-bodied citizens, male and female, enrolled in the inittial baccalaureate degree courses; prescribes the service components of the Program as follows: (1) Military Training Service; (2) Civic Welfare Services; (3) Law Enforcement Service; and (4) Community Development Services. Provides penal sanctions.
